Light 0.0.5 improves portable exports and conflict handling while returning the editor to a focused WYSIWYG-only experience.

## Portable single-note exports

- Exporting one note now includes every referenced local image, audio file, video, document, and other attachment.
- Folder exports also include attachments referenced from outside the selected folder.
- Unrelated attachments and linked Markdown notes are not pulled into a single-note archive.
- Full-vault exports now preserve all user files, including attachment types that do not appear in the document tree.

## Git-style text merging

- Smart merge is now the default conflict policy for new S3 configurations.
- Light uses the last synchronized object as a merge base and automatically combines non-overlapping edits without requiring Git to be installed.
- Overlapping Markdown and plain-text edits use standard local/base/remote conflict markers so no text is silently discarded.
- Structured JSON documents such as boards and canvases are merged only when the result remains valid; unsafe conflicts conservatively fall back to keeping both versions.
- Binary files, missing merge bases, invalid UTF-8, and oversized files also fall back to the existing keep-both behavior.

## Editor and outline

- Removed the split source/preview mode and its saved preference. Light now provides one consistent WYSIWYG editor.
- Restored the centered document width and removed all mode-switch UI and unused preview code.
- Long outline entries wrap within the sidebar instead of overflowing or being clipped.

## Quality

- Added regression coverage for single-note attachment exports, clean and conflicting three-way merges, structured-file fallbacks, and sync convergence.
- Passed 1,058 automated frontend tests, the production web build, and the native Rust/Tauri check before release.

## Downloads

- Windows x64 — NSIS installer
- Linux x64 — AppImage and Debian package
- macOS Apple Silicon — application bundle and DMG
- macOS Intel — application bundle and DMG

Installers are attached as each platform's build completes. The binaries are not code-signed yet; Windows and macOS may display a warning on first launch.
